publicly_readable: One article, reprinted on worldin.economist.com in 2015 for the 30th edition ("AIDS casts a dark shadow", by Matt Ridley), read from an Internet Archive snapshot.
not_readable: Everything else in the issue. No other text of this edition was found in public form.

entries.quote: In 1988, AIDS will break two gruesome records. It will be ten years since the first cases were recognised (retrospectively) in America and Belgium; and the number of people known to have caught it will pass 100,000 for the first time.
entries.subject: Reported AIDS cases worldwide

entries.quote: The threat of a heterosexual epidemic in America and Europe will begin to recede.
entries.subject: Heterosexual AIDS epidemic in America and Europe

entries.quote: The World in 1988 foresaw major changes in central Europe, especially in East Germany—a year out, but pretty close.
entries.subject: Change in central Europe
entries.note: Restated in "Looking back on the future" (The World in 2006), a review by an outside historian; the original wording is not seen.

notes: Edition number counted from The World in 1987 = 1. Publication month not confirmed; year only. The reprint is The Economist's own web copy of the original article.
